title: Predicting student dropout from virtual learning environment activity
abstract: We model weekly click-stream activity of first-year students with gradient boosting and survival analysis to flag students at risk of dropping out, and evaluate the early-warning system on three cohorts.

title: Item response theory for short multiple-choice quizzes
abstract: We compare Rasch and two-parameter logistic models for quizzes with fewer than twenty items and show how small samples bias discrimination estimates.

title: Transformer models for Sinhala text classification
abstract: We fine-tune multilingual transformer models on a new corpus of Sinhala news articles and study tokenisation choices for a low-resource language.

title: Detecting electricity theft with smart meter data
abstract: Unsupervised anomaly detection on daily consumption profiles, combined with transformer-level energy balance, ranks customers for inspection.

title: Fair exam timetabling with simulated annealing
abstract: Kempe-chain moves inside simulated annealing spread students' exams across the exam period without clashes on university benchmark instances.

title: Explainable credit scoring for microfinance
abstract: We train gradient boosted trees on loan repayment records and use SHAP values to explain decisions to loan officers in rural branches.

title: Active learning for systematic review screening
abstract: Ranking titles and abstracts with naive Bayes during screening finds relevant studies early; a hypergeometric stopping rule decides when to stop.

title: Forecasting hospital bed demand with hierarchical time series
abstract: We reconcile ward-level and hospital-level forecasts of bed occupancy and compare ETS, ARIMA and gradient boosting baselines.

title: Measuring teaching quality with student feedback text
abstract: Topic models and sentiment analysis of open-ended course feedback reveal which aspects of teaching students comment on most.

title: Graph neural networks for course prerequisite discovery
abstract: We learn prerequisite relations between university courses from syllabi and enrolment sequences using graph neural networks.

title: Plagiarism detection in programming assignments
abstract: Token-based greedy string tiling with class-relative thresholds detects copied code that was renamed, reordered or padded.

title: Bayesian A/B testing for e-learning interface changes
abstract: A hierarchical Bayesian model of completion rates lets an online course platform stop experiments early with calibrated risk.
